A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a lesion of the visual pathway leads to a decrease of functional connections, which is compensated by an increase in long range inter-network connections, with the exception of the Visual Network.
the brain of hemianopic patients is characterized by a less compact network structure, with a reduced functional segregation and a higher functional specialization.
the hemianopic brain is characterized by a general decrease in functional connectivity, which is more prominent in the VN.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the brain functional organization in hemianopic individuals is less organized, characterized by a lower functional integration and by a higher segregation of functional networks.

functional connectivity is a powerful tool to investigate the neural basis of visual awareness, providing a novel approach in the study of hemianopia and in the assessment of the neural basis of the blindsight.
functional reorganization after brain injury is not limited to the lesioned area, but it is a widespread phenomenon that affects the entire brain.
